reason: We are at the penultimate iteration and the simulation runs end-to-end, but there are still major logic and specification gaps that materially affect results (mandate-aware mobility bug, enforcement inactive without disease, missing key metrics and parameter mappings). One more focused iteration can deliver substantial accuracy and spec-alignment improvements with contained code changes.

specific_areas: Fix mandate-aware public-space attendance: pass mandate_active into _attend_locations_today and enforce location capacity
Apply enforcement filtering regardless of disease mode; consistently count enforcement actions
Map config aliases: rewire_prob -> rewiring_prob_small_world and daily_contacts_home/work/community -> contact_rate_by_location
Add time-to-threshold metrics for 70% and 90% adoption
Implement restock_interval_days and enforce retailer.rationing_limit_per_person in purchases; track daily stockouts and unmet demand to compute supply_shortage_days
Use Person.susceptibility_to_social_influence in the decision rule; deduplicate social ties after network generation
Introduce a minimal RiskEnvironment class to broadcast risk (wrapper around current risk update) and integrate it
Replace placeholder information_impact with a basic elasticity estimate using variation in campaign intensity
Remove redundant pass statements and the unused np_rng (or actually use it); gate visualization behind a config flag

task_understanding.adjustments: Re-emphasize strict alignment with the provided specification: mandates must affect mobility and enforcement independent of disease; include the RiskEnvironment entity; ensure all specified metrics (time-to-threshold 70/90, supply shortages) are implemented.

data_analysis.adjustments: Instrument the simulation to record daily retailer stockouts/unmet demand, campaign intensity, misinformation exposure, and enforcement events to enable computation of supply_shortage_days and information_impact elasticity.

model_planning.adjustments: Prioritize high-impact, low-risk fixes for the final iteration: mandate-aware mobility, enforcement applicability, metrics completion, and config mapping. Implement a minimal RiskEnvironment wrapper rather than a complex redesign.

code_generation.adjustments: Implement the concrete diffs: pass mandate_active to attendance, enforce capacity, unify enforcement filtering, map config aliases, add time-to-70/90, honor restock_interval_days, enforce retailer.rationing_limit_per_person by default, apply susceptibility in decision, deduplicate social ties, add RiskEnvironment class and integrate.

code_verification.adjustments: Add targeted assertions/tests: (1) With mandates on, public-space attendance decreases; (2) Enforcement filters out some unmasked attendees in mandate locations even without disease; (3) Restock occurs only on interval boundaries; (4) daily_contacts_* correctly influences contact rates; (5) time_to_reach_70_percent and 90% populated when thresholds are crossed; (6) supply_shortage_days increments on any retailer stockout.

simulation_execution.adjustments: Run small seeded tests in both disease-disabled and disease-enabled modes to validate enforcement and mobility changes; stress-test public-space capacity with high attendance probabilities; ensure no crashes with new metrics collection.

result_evaluation.adjustments: Report complete metrics: time_to_reach_50/70/90, supply_shortage_days, both-masked contact share, policy effect with and without enforcement, and a basic information_impact elasticity. Verify non-placeholder values and sanity-check trends.

feedback_generation.adjustments: Provide a concise, prioritized summary of changes, note remaining limitations (e.g., simplified RiskEnvironment), and include brief code references to where each change was made for traceability.
